query: For high-entropy alloys intended for harsh corrosive mechanical environments, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion, and why? Propose a controlled comparison that would test the hypothesis, predict how combined degradation and its wear and corrosion components would differ from a matched baseline, define where the prediction should hold or fail, identify supporting prior evidence, and state an observation that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Under simultaneous wear and corrosion in high-entropy alloys, resistance is governed by the dynamic formation and self-healing of a protective tribo-oxide film whose stability is enhanced by alloying elements such as Al and Ti; this film reduces both mechanical removal and electrochemical dissolution under sliding in corrosive media.
generation.intervention: Alloying addition of 0.5 at% Al and 0.2 at% Ti to produce CoCrFeNiAl0.5Ti0.2
generation.conditions: Reciprocating sliding at 5 N normal load, 5 mm/s stroke speed, in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution at pH 7 and 25 °C
generation.structural_mediator: Adherent, self-healing Al- and Ti-enriched oxide tribo-film on the sliding surface
generation.mechanism: Al and Ti promote rapid re-passivation under mechanical disruption, forming a dense oxide layer that impedes both plowing/wear and anodic metal dissolution, thus reducing synergistic degradation
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to undoped CoCrFeNi: combined wear + corrosion loss reduced by ~30%; wear-only volume loss reduced by ~20%; steady-state corrosion current density reduced by ~50%.
generation.baseline: Undoped CoCrFeNi alloy tested under identical sliding-corrosion conditions
generation.boundary: Prediction should hold for pH≥6 and sliding speeds ≤10 mm/s; expected to fail at pH≤4 where aggressive acid attack overwhelms the oxide’s protective ability
generation.uncertainty: Moderate—effect-size estimates are extrapolated from passive-film studies but lack direct wear-corrosion synergy data for this specific alloy system

falsification_experiment.design: Perform reciprocating sliding wear tests on CoCrFeNi and CoCrFeNiAl0.5Ti0.2 specimens in 3.5 wt% NaCl at pH 7, 25 °C, under 5 N load and 5 mm/s, while continuously recording electrochemical current.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If CoCrFeNiAl0.5Ti0.2 exhibits <10% reduction in combined material loss relative to baseline and shows no measurable improvement in oxide film continuity or Al/Ti enrichment, the hypothesis is falsified.
